def test_bucket_sort_nominal():
    unsorted = [0.42, 0.32, 0.33, 0.52, 0.37, 0.47, 0.51]
    sorted_list = bucket_sort(unsorted, bucket_count=5)
    assert sorted_list == [0.32, 0.33, 0.37, 0.42, 0.47, 0.51, 0.52]


def test_bucket_sort_integers():
    unsorted = [55, 12, 42, 3, 19, 88]
    sorted_list = bucket_sort(unsorted, bucket_count=4)
    assert sorted_list == [3, 12, 19, 42, 55, 88]


def test_bucket_sort_boundary_max_value():
    # Kills arithmetic and boundary mutants (mutmut_12, mutmut_13, mutmut_22, mutmut_23, mutmut_25)
    unsorted = [1, 10]
    sorted_list = bucket_sort(unsorted, bucket_count=3)
    assert sorted_list == [1, 10]


def test_bucket_sort_multiple_elements_spanning_buckets():
    # This specifically targets arithmetic in bucket_size calculation and index determination,
    # as well as ensuring max_value element maps to bucket_count - 1 (killing mutmut_25).
    unsorted = [0, 5, 10]
    # With bucket_count=2, bucket_size = (10 - 0) / 2 = 5.0.
    # Elements: 
    # 0 -> index = min(int((0 - 0)/5.0), 1) = 0
    # 5 -> index = min(int((5 - 0)/5.0), 1) = min(1, 1) = 1
    # 10 -> index = min(int((10 - 0)/5.0), 1) = min(2, 1) = 1
    assert bucket_sort(unsorted, bucket_count=2) == [0, 5, 10]
